memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people rose and stood at the entrances to their tents, watching Moses until he entered the tent. As Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stay at the entrance, while the Lord spoke with Moses." - Exod 33:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Picture the scene. Moses walks out toward the tent, and the whole camp stops. Every family stands at their own doorway and watches. Then the cloud descends, and God speaks with one man.

There is longing in that image, but also distance. They watched. They did not enter. They saw the cloud from far off while another man went in to speak with God.

Under the old covenant, that was the arrangement. Access was mediated, limited, and largely observed from a distance.

What a mercy that this is not our position. Every believer in Christ has been given access by one Spirit to the Father (Eph 2:18). We are not spectators at the tent door. Through Jesus, we come in.

And yet — how often do we live like the people at the doorway? We watch others pray, listen to others speak of God's nearness, admire a preacher or a friend whose walk seems deep, and quietly assume that closeness with God is for people like them.

It is not. The curtain is torn. You are not meant to stand in the doorway watching someone else meet with God. Go in.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as a spectator of other people's faith?
2. What holds you back from approaching God yourself?
3. When did you last speak with God honestly and unhurriedly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not want to watch from a distance. Thank You that in Christ I may come in. Amen.
